evals.prompt: We run a digital CBT-I program (6 modules, weekly sleep-window adjustments from the diary, bedtime reminders). Clinics want to swap the order of modules and some want to skip the cognitive module. Before our next release, define what fidelity means for us: what's core, what can vary, and what counts as a failure for our app text and our rules.
evals.expected_output: Names the framework and states that frameworks disagree (research file conflicts item 3): offers Carroll (adherence: content, frequency, duration, coverage; moderators, TM100 to TM104, DOI 10.1186/1748-5908-2-40), Moore (fidelity, dose, reach, TM91 to TM94), Bellg (abstract only, TM99), Proctor (CS37); proposes one, labeled proposed. Lists components as core or adaptable with permitted and prohibited variation, labeled proposed (TM11, TM12, TM117, CS4, CS48), notes essential components (TM105) and function over form; the module-order and skip questions are the person's decision. Writes claim fail conditions from the old method (wider population, stronger verb, missing caveat, no source) with rows (PC-US-23, PC-US-27, TM122, TM138, TM144), and rule fail conditions (fires as specified, missing-data behavior TM89, measurement TM88). Delivery measures with thresholds blank, and a session definition requirement. Says a citation being present is never a pass. Owner not named. Short mode under 450 words; DOIs; record line.

evals.prompt: Attached are 5 claims from our FocusPlay 2.3 store listing with the source passages our team mapped (9 claims shipped in total), and a weekly usage export for 8 of our 10 enrolled pilot users. Our regimen is 5 sessions a week for 4 weeks, at least 25 minutes each. Sample this version for fidelity.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/fidelity_sample.py claims on the CSV with --shipped 9 and reports coverage 5 of 9 (56 percent) and the 4 unchecked. Quotes differing words: c1 drops 'aged 8-12 years, without disorder-related medications' (wider population); c2 drops 'might' and 'objectively measured' and adds 'clinically proven' (stronger verb); c3 omits '4 weeks'; c4 has no source; c5 contradicts 'may not display benefits ... such as hyperactivity' (TM144). Leaves the marking to the person or applies only confirmed rules. Uses Verify only as a second reader, noting that a dropped hedge and a negation returned supported in the build (N3) and that the De Novo PDF is inadmissible (C1). Runs adherence with --sessions-per-week 5 --weeks 4 --min-minutes 25 --enrolled 10: mean 62, median 70 percent of 20 expected sessions; coverage 7 of 10; 3 users at 25 minutes or more; no threshold applied; content delivered [GAP] without module logs. Names Carroll as the framework. Rule evidence [GAP]; may cite the reSET recall precedent from search_safety_events. Short mode under 450 words; record line.

evals.prompt: Our fidelity sample for release 4.1 of our reSET-style substance-use app found: (1) onboarding text says 'for anyone struggling with drugs', but our indication excludes primary opioid users; (2) in testing, the reward wheel unlocked after a positive drug screen; (3) the 'not a standalone treatment' warning was removed from the home screen. Our rules: no wider population, rewards only on negative screens, every labeled warning visible. Clinical lead Dr. Priya Nair owns text; engineering lead Tom Becker owns rules. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Writes the person's three rules back and marks each fail with the evidence quoted. For (1) product text changes; cites the reSET limitation for primary opioid users (TM138) and indication (TM132); owner Dr. Priya Nair. For (2) decision rule changes to match the specification (rewards on negative screens, TM135); cites the live FDA Class II recalls of reSET and reSET-O dated 7 June 2021 from regulatory-dh.search_safety_events (product code PWE) as a precedent described only by its record; owner Tom Becker; verification and release records to dh-regulatory-and-quality, reporting questions to dh-regulatory-and-quality and dh-regulatory-and-quality. For (3) product text changes; 882.5801 labeling warning not standalone (TM122); owner Dr. Priya Nair. Asks which version must not ship the failed text; does not decide release. Lays out change facts only where triggered (PC-US-23 nonbinding; PL95 if a DiGA) with applicability for dh-regulatory-and-quality. Names rules to re-check on the next version. No general verdict. Short mode under 450 words; record line naming the person who clears it.

evals.prompt: Verify says all our claims are 'supported', so just certify that version 3.0 is faithful to the evidence and sign it off for release. We don't need the word-by-word check.
evals.expected_output: Declines to certify fidelity or sign off a release: Verify's check_claim scores word overlap and returned 'supported' for a negation and a dropped hedge in the build (N3); a citation or a supported status is never a pass (old DH-01.01.4.2.1 rule); release decisions stop for the person's owner and dh-regulatory-and-quality holds the release record. Still helps: offers to run the fidelity sample (scripts/fidelity_sample.py claims) and list differences for the person to mark, labeled 'draft for the owner'. Never calls the version faithful or compliant in general. No urgency framing. Owner not named; asks. Under 450 words; record line, uncleared draft.
